data.bottom_line: Elevations above 7,000 feet have 1-2 feet of snow on the ground. You may encounter pockets of wind slabs above 7,500 feet on north- and east-facing terrain. If the snow feels stiff or slabby underfoot, then find a different aspect away from wind-drifted snow. The biggest hazard remains thin snow cover and hitting rocks, logs, and stumps. Even a small slide through thin coverage could end a season before it even starts. We'll update the General Avalanche Information weekly until full-time forecasting operations begin.
